title: OAuth2 connection requires reauthorization — token expired or revoked
problem: The OAuth2 access token stored in a Make connection is no longer valid. Make attempts to use the refresh token to obtain a new access token, but if the refresh token is also expired or revoked, the authentication fails and all scenarios using this connection return 401 errors from the external service.
symptoms: Scenario was working for an extended period and suddenly starts failing on every execution
All modules using the same connection fail simultaneously
Make may show a warning indicator on the connection in the Connections list

likely_causes.cause: The OAuth2 refresh token has expired due to inactivity — many providers expire refresh tokens after a defined period of non-use
The user changed their password on the external service, which some providers use to invalidate all OAuth tokens
The user revoked the Make application's access in the external service's connected apps settings
The OAuth2 scope or permissions were changed on the external service, invalidating the existing token

diagnosis_steps: Go to Make > Connections and locate the connection used by the failing modules
Look for a warning indicator or error status on the connection
Attempt to reauthorize the connection by clicking the Reauthorize option
If reauthorization fails, read the exact error message — it will indicate whether the issue is an expired token, revoked access, or another problem
Log into the external service and check whether the Make app still appears in the authorized or connected apps list

solutions.solution: Click Reauthorize on the failing connection in Make > Connections and complete the OAuth2 authorization flow again
solutions.conditions: Standard fix — works when the account is still active and the Make app authorization was not explicitly revoked

solutions.solution: Delete the existing connection and create a new one from scratch
solutions.conditions: When Reauthorize fails or the connection state is unrecoverable

solutions.solution: After creating a new connection, update all scenarios that used the old connection to use the new one
solutions.conditions: Required step after creating a replacement connection

prevention: Use dedicated service accounts or bot accounts for Make connections rather than personal accounts, to avoid disruption from password changes
Set up Make scenario failure notifications to detect authentication failures immediately when they occur
Maintain a documented inventory of which accounts are used for each connection

origin_details.evidence: Type corrected from make_core to make_core (retained) because the connection management is Make's responsibility, but the token expiry originates from the external service's OAuth2 policy. Origin correctly set to external_service. The previous version's type=make_core is debatable — the connection infrastructure is Make, but the token lifecycle policy is external. Retained make_core because it is surfaced through Make's connection system. The claim that 'many providers expire refresh tokens after 30-90 days' from the previous version was removed as the specific duration varies widely and was not confirmed.

title: Make connection is invalid or broken — all modules using it fail
problem: A Make connection shows as invalid or broken. All scenarios and modules that use this connection fail immediately on execution.
symptoms: A warning or error indicator is visible on the connection in Make > Connections
All scenarios using this connection fail at the first module that uses it
Connection verification test returns an error
The error references the connection explicitly rather than a specific data value

likely_causes.cause: OAuth2 access and refresh tokens have both expired or been revoked
API key was deleted or rotated in the external service without updating the Make connection
The account used to create the connection was deleted or suspended in the external service
The external service changed its authentication endpoint or API version, breaking existing connections

diagnosis_steps: Go to Make > Connections and find all connections with a warning or error indicator
Click on the connection and attempt to verify it
Read the exact error message shown during connection verification
Log into the external service and verify that the account still exists and is active
Check whether the Make application still appears in the external service's authorized apps list

solutions.solution: Attempt to reauthorize the connection by using the Reauthorize or reconnect option in the connection settings
solutions.conditions: When the issue is an expired OAuth token and the account is still valid

solutions.solution: Generate a new API key in the external service and update or recreate the Make connection with the new key
solutions.conditions: When the connection uses API key authentication and the key was rotated or deleted

solutions.solution: Delete the connection and create a new one with valid credentials
solutions.conditions: When reauthorization fails or the connection cannot be recovered

prevention: Use service accounts with stable credentials for Make connections
Monitor connection health by setting up scenario failure notifications
Maintain a connection inventory documenting the account and credential type for each connection

origin_details.evidence: This entry partially overlaps with auth-oauth2-token-expired. They are kept separate because: this entry describes the Make-side connection state (generic broken connection) while auth-oauth2-token-expired focuses on the OAuth2 token lifecycle mechanism. The two have different diagnostic paths. A user seeing 'connection is invalid' may not know it is an OAuth issue. Origin corrected to external_service — the root cause is typically external credentials becoming invalid.

title: OAuth2 connection missing required scope for the requested action
problem: A Make connection was authorized with a set of OAuth2 scopes that does not include the permission required for a new module or action being added to the scenario. The external API returns 403 Forbidden when the action is attempted.
symptoms: A newly added module fails while existing modules using the same connection still work
The error is consistent and not data-dependent
Error started after adding a new feature or module to the scenario

likely_causes.cause: The connection was authorized before the new action was added to the scenario, and the new action requires a scope that was not granted at authorization time
The user did not grant all requested scopes during the OAuth2 authorization flow (some providers allow partial scope acceptance)

diagnosis_steps: Read the error message carefully — it typically identifies the missing scope by name
Check the external service's API documentation to confirm which scope is required for the failing action
Go to Make > Connections and review which scopes are shown as granted for this connection
Check the external service's connected apps settings to see the exact permissions granted to Make

solutions.solution: Delete the existing connection and create a new one, carefully granting all required scopes during the OAuth2 authorization step — refer to the API documentation to identify the necessary scopes for all actions used in the workflow
solutions.conditions: When the connection is missing a required scope and re-authorization with updated scopes is needed

prevention: Before creating a Make connection, review the API documentation to identify the scopes required by all modules and actions you plan to use in the workflow
Grant the scopes required by all planned modules and actions — not broader, not narrower
Test new modules against the existing connection before going to production to detect scope issues early

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Connections and OAuth2
origin_details.evidence: OAuth2 scope management by Make connections is documented. The specific claim that some providers allow partial scope acceptance during authorization is correct for some providers (Google, for example) but not all — this was originally stated as a general rule and is now framed as a possibility. The previous prevention advice ('grant broadest reasonable scopes') has been corrected — granting broader scopes than needed is a security risk and is inconsistent with the principle of least privilege.

title: API Key authentication failure
problem: A Make module using API Key authentication fails because the API key configured in the Make connection is invalid, has been rotated, deleted, has expired (if the provider supports key expiry), or does not have the required permissions for the API endpoint being called.
symptoms: Module fails immediately on every execution
All modules in the scenario using this API key fail simultaneously
Error started after a key rotation or account change in the external service
A newly created API key still causes failure

likely_causes.cause: The API key was deleted or regenerated in the external service's dashboard without updating the Make connection
The API key value was entered incorrectly in the Make connection (extra whitespace, truncation)
The API key does not have the required permissions or scopes for the endpoint being called
The API key is being passed in the wrong location for this specific API (wrong header name, or should be a query parameter instead)

diagnosis_steps: Go to Make > Connections and find the API key connection
Verify the API key value by copying it fresh from the external service's dashboard to eliminate copy-paste errors
Test the API key directly using Postman or curl to confirm it works outside of Make
Verify the correct header name or query parameter name for the API key in the external service's API documentation
Check whether the API key has the required permissions in the external service's dashboard

solutions.solution: Delete the Make connection and create a new one with the current, valid API key copied fresh from the external service dashboard
solutions.conditions: When the key was rotated or was entered with an error

solutions.solution: Generate a new API key with the correct permissions in the external service and update the Make connection with it
solutions.conditions: When the existing key was deleted or has insufficient permissions

solutions.solution: Verify the API key placement: check whether the key should be in the Authorization header, a custom header (e.g., X-API-Key), or as a query parameter, and correct the HTTP module or connection configuration
solutions.conditions: When using the HTTP module directly with manual header configuration and the key location may be wrong

prevention: Store API keys in Make connections rather than hardcoded in HTTP module headers or body
Document API key rotation procedures and update Make connections immediately after any rotation
Test the API key in Postman before entering it in Make to confirm it is valid

origin_details.evidence: API key connection management in Make is documented. Origin corrected to external_service — the 401/403 is returned by the external service when it rejects the key. The previous version cited 'API key expired' as an error message — removed because not all providers support key expiry, and it was presented as a general message without source confirmation.
